wake_01.speaker: narrator
wake_01.text: You come back to yourself one sense at a time. Taste first — copper, and grit.

wake_02.speaker: narrator
wake_02.text: Then the cold. You are lying face-down in a field that was a wheat field this morning.

wake_03.speaker: narrator
wake_03.text: Then the quiet. That is the part that gets you upright.

wake_04.speaker: narrator
wake_04.text: Nine hundred men were screaming here. Now there is wind, and something far off that is burning without crackling.

wake_05.speaker: narrator
wake_05.text: Kharwyn Hold is still on the ridge where it has been for four hundred years. Most of it.

wake_06.speaker: narrator
wake_06.text: You were on the east wall. The east wall is a mile behind you and you do not remember walking.

first_choice.prompt: Your brother was on the east wall with you.

options.text: Stay low. Whatever is out here can hear you too.
Look at the Hold first. Understand what happened.

call_out_01.speaker: narrator
call_out_01.text: Your voice goes out across the field and nothing sends it back. No echo. The sound just stops, four feet from your mouth, like it hit a wall.

call_out_02.speaker: narrator
call_out_02.text: You have shouted across this valley since you were eleven years old. It has always answered.

stay_quiet_01.speaker: narrator
stay_quiet_01.text: You stay down and count to thirty, the way Sergeant Merrick taught you. Merrick is nineteen feet to your left with his helm on and nothing inside it.

stay_quiet_02.speaker: narrator
stay_quiet_02.text: Nothing moves in thirty. So you move.

look_hold_01.speaker: narrator
look_hold_01.text: The curtain wall is intact. The gatehouse is intact. The banners are still flying, both crowns, on the same pole, which means somebody hoisted them and then nobody came to argue about it.

look_hold_02.speaker: narrator
look_hold_02.text: The keep is gone. Not fallen — gone. There is a hole where the undercroft was, and the hole is the wrong shape for anything a siege engine does.

look_hold_03.speaker: narrator
look_hold_03.text: It goes down. You are a long way away and you can still tell it goes down further than the mountain is tall.

converge_01.speaker: narrator
converge_01.text: Somebody has been through this field already. The dead are in rows, and there are crosses.

converge_02.speaker: narrator
converge_02.text: Crosses take time. Which means this did not happen an hour ago, whatever your body thinks.

converge_03.speaker: narrator
converge_03.text: Then, forty feet out, one of the rows moves.

find_cael_01.speaker: narrator
find_cael_01.text: A hand, working at the dirt. Not clawing. Turning something over, patiently, the way he used to worry at a knot.

find_cael_02.speaker: narrator
find_cael_02.text: Cael is nineteen and he has never been able to sit still, not once, not in church, not at their mother's burial.

find_cael_03.speaker: narrator
find_cael_03.text: He is sitting very still now.

find_cael_07.speaker: brother
find_cael_07.text: I don't know. I don't think that's the — please don't come over here.

reveal_02.speaker: narrator
reveal_02.text: There is light coming out of them. Not fire. It doesn't flicker and it doesn't warm the air and it is the colour of nothing you have a word for.

reveal_03.speaker: narrator
reveal_03.text: Father Aldric taught the two of you your catechism in a stone room with a low ceiling. The Devouring comes as a gift, he said. That is how you will know it. It will arrive looking like a gift.

reveal_04.speaker: brother
reveal_04.text: It started three days ago. It stops sometimes. Then it doesn't.

reveal_05.speaker: brother
reveal_05.text: I've been sitting here because I thought if I sat here long enough it would go and I could just — walk back and not have to say it out loud.

react_choice.prompt: He is waiting. He has been waiting three days.

options.text: "You're my brother. That's all this changes."
"There's a rite for this. Father Aldric knew it."
"Tell me exactly what happened under the Hold."

react_reassure.speaker: narrator
react_reassure.text: Cael's shoulders come down about an inch. It is the first ordinary thing his body has done since you found him.

react_reassure_03.speaker: brother
react_reassure_03.text: But thank you for saying it fast. You didn't have to say it fast.

react_recoil.speaker: narrator
react_recoil.text: He goes very still again. He nods, several times, as though you have confirmed something he worked out days ago and was hoping to be wrong about.

react_recoil_03.speaker: brother
react_recoil_03.text: I'll stay here, then. You should go and find your unit.

react_faith.speaker: brother
react_faith.text: A rite. You want to say words over me.

react_faith_02.speaker: brother
react_faith_02.text: Aldric is under nine feet of the keep. Whatever he knew, he knew it about something that hadn't happened yet.

react_faith_03.speaker: narrator
react_faith_03.text: He is right, and being right does not seem to be any comfort to him at all.

react_ask.speaker: brother
react_ask.text: The floor opened. That's not a figure of speech, it opened, like a mouth, and everything went down.

react_ask_02.speaker: brother
react_ask_02.text: And while I was falling something spoke. Not words. But it was speaking, and it was speaking to me specifically, and I answered it.

react_ask_03.speaker: brother
react_ask_03.text: I don't know what I agreed to. That's the part I can't stop thinking about.

react_silence_02.speaker: narrator
react_silence_02.text: The silence goes on long enough to become an answer, and both of you hear it become one.

react_silence_03.speaker: brother
react_silence_03.text: That's all right. I'd have taken a while too.

harrow_01.speaker: narrator
harrow_01.text: A voice behind you, flat and close and much too near for someone you did not hear approach.

harrow_02.speaker: medic
harrow_02.text: Aldrethi. Good. Step to your left and keep stepping.

harrow_03.speaker: narrator
harrow_03.text: Field medic. Aldrethi green under three days of other people's blood. He has a bonesaw in his right hand and he is holding it the way you hold a weapon, not the way you hold a tool.

harrow_04.speaker: medic
harrow_04.text: I've buried forty-one men in this field. Six of them were lit up like that when I found them. None of them stayed men very long.

harrow_05.speaker: brother
harrow_05.text: I'm right here. You can say it to me.

harrow_06.speaker: medic
harrow_06.text: I know you're right there, son. That's the problem I'm solving.

harrow_07.speaker: narrator
harrow_07.text: He has not looked at you once. He is watching Cael's hands the way you watch a dog you have already decided about.

harrow_choice.prompt: The bonesaw hasn't moved. Neither has he.

options.text: "Six out of how many? You don't know either."
"He's not Marked. He's carrying a Vaethari lamp he stripped off a sapper."

options.locked_text: Step to your left. [You already told him he was your brother]

harrow_shield.speaker: narrator
harrow_shield.text: You move. It is not a decision so much as a thing your legs do while the rest of you is still arguing.

harrow_shield_03.speaker: medic
harrow_shield_03.text: Brothers. Should have seen it — you've got the same jaw. That makes this harder, and it doesn't make it different.

harrow_shield_04.speaker: narrator
harrow_shield_04.text: He lowers the saw. Not far. About as far as a man lowers a thing he expects to raise again.

harrow_reason.speaker: medic
harrow_reason.text: Six out of six. That's how many I've seen. You want to tell me the number that makes six out of six acceptable odds, I'll listen.

harrow_reason_02.speaker: narrator
harrow_reason_02.text: It is not a good argument. It is not a stupid one either, and that is the trouble with all of this — nobody here has anything better than what they have seen with their own eyes.

harrow_reason_03.speaker: medic
harrow_reason_03.text: But you're right that I don't know. I'll grant you that much, and I'll grant it standing exactly where I'm standing.

harrow_lie.speaker: narrator
harrow_lie.text: The lie comes out level and easy and you have no idea where you learned to do that.

harrow_lie_02.speaker: narrator
harrow_lie_02.text: Cael's face does something complicated. He closes his hands.

harrow_lie_04.speaker: medic
harrow_lie_04.text: Vaethari make good lamps. That'd be the first sensible thing I've heard in three days.

harrow_lie_05.speaker: narrator
harrow_lie_05.text: He does not believe you. He wants to, which is not the same thing, and for now he is choosing to behave as though he does.

harrow_aside_02.speaker: narrator
harrow_aside_02.text: Cael does not say anything about it. He watches you do it, and then he keeps watching the place where you were.

harrow_aside_04.speaker: narrator
harrow_aside_04.text: He does not use the saw. He was, it turns out, waiting to see what you would do. You will not know for a long time whether that was a test you failed.

harrow_timeout.speaker: narrator
harrow_timeout.text: You are still deciding when Harrow stops waiting for you to.

harrow_timeout_02.speaker: medic
harrow_timeout_02.text: That's all right. Most men freeze. It's the ones who move fast you have to worry about.

harrow_timeout_03.speaker: narrator
harrow_timeout_03.text: He lowers the saw himself, on his own schedule, having established whose schedule it is.

deduce_setup_01.speaker: medic
deduce_setup_01.text: Since we're all standing here being reasonable. Somebody opened that undercroft. I'd like to know who, because I'd like to know whether they can do it again.

deduce_setup_02.speaker: medic
deduce_setup_02.text: Vaethari sappers had been digging under that wall for six weeks. I pulled two of them out of the rubble myself, still in their harness, four hundred feet from where any tunnel of theirs should have ended.

deduce_setup_03.speaker: narrator
deduce_setup_03.text: There was a Vaethari sapper alive in this field yesterday, according to Harrow. He was not alive by the time Harrow finished with his leg.

deduce_setup_04.speaker: medic
deduce_setup_04.text: He kept saying the same thing over and over. Didn't make sense then. Doesn't now.

deduce_setup_05.speaker: medic
deduce_setup_05.text: He said: we never got that deep. He said it in Aldrethi so I'd understand him. That's a thing a man does when he wants to be believed.

deduce_setup_06.speaker: narrator
deduce_setup_06.text: Three accounts. None of them can be checked. All of them come from people with a reason to be wrong.

deduce_01.question: Who opened the undercroft at Kharwyn Hold?
deduce_01.commit_prompt: Your conclusion — you will act on this:

statements.text: Vaethari sappers had been digging under that wall for six weeks. I pulled two out of the rubble myself.
While I was falling, something spoke. And I answered it.

options.text: The Vaethari did it. They dug too far and they broke something.
Somebody was down there before the siege. The sappers only found the door.

effects.remember_text: You have started keeping your own counsel.

options.text: It was already awake. It opened itself, and it picked someone to talk to.
options.locked_text: [Something Cael said — but you never asked him what happened]

options.text: Say you don't know. Three days is not long enough to know anything.

deduce_vaethari.speaker: medic
deduce_vaethari.text: That's what I think too. Which ought to worry both of us, because I've been wrong about everything else this week.

deduce_earlier.speaker: narrator
deduce_earlier.text: You keep the thought behind your teeth. If somebody sealed that thing in, somebody knew it was there, and knowing where it is has been somebody's job for a very long time.

deduce_earlier_02.speaker: medic
deduce_earlier_02.text: You've gone quiet. That's usually a man deciding not to tell me something.

deduce_cael.speaker: narrator
deduce_cael.text: Cael's head comes up. It is the first time since you found him that he has looked at you as though you were on the same side of something.

deduce_cael_02.speaker: medic
deduce_cael_02.text: That's not a theory, that's a sermon. I've had enough of those.

deduce_nothing.speaker: medic
deduce_nothing.text: Good. Hold onto that. Everybody who's certain right now is about to get somebody killed.

tremor_02.speaker: narrator
tremor_02.text: Not shaking. Soft, for a quarter of a second, the way ice goes soft before it stops being ice.

tremor_03.speaker: medic
tremor_03.text: Tremor. Down, get down, hands off the ground —

tremor_04.speaker: narrator
tremor_04.text: Forty feet away, a row of the dead sits up together. All of them. At the same time, with the same movement, like one thing wearing eleven bodies.

tremor_05.speaker: narrator
tremor_05.text: The colour goes out of everything. Not dark — colourless, as though something is standing between the field and the idea of light.

tremor_07.speaker: brother
tremor_07.text: It's the same one. It's the same one that spoke.

escape_clean_01.speaker: narrator
escape_clean_01.text: You get a fist in his collar and haul, and his weight comes with you, and the ground where he was sitting is not ground any more.

escape_hurt_01.speaker: narrator
escape_hurt_01.text: You are slow. Something closes on your leg below the knee, without heat, without pressure, and takes a piece of it out of the world.

escape_hurt_02.speaker: narrator
escape_hurt_02.text: Then Cael's hands are on you, both of them, lit up, and whatever had your leg lets go of it the way a hand lets go of a hot pan.

escape_hurt_03.speaker: narrator
escape_hurt_03.text: Your brother drags you thirty feet through a wheat field with a hand that is not a hand right now, and you will be thinking about that for a long time.

escape_converge_01.speaker: narrator
escape_converge_01.text: The three of you go over the treeline and keep going until the field is out of sight and then further, because none of you wants to be the one who says stop.

close_02.speaker: medic
close_02.text: Right. New information. That's twice now I've seen the dead get up, and both times there was one of the lit ones within a hundred feet.

close_03.speaker: medic
close_03.text: I'm not saying he called it. I'm saying I've stopped being able to tell the difference between a man a thing wants and a man who's holding the door for it.

close_04.speaker: medic
close_04.text: There's a word going round for people like your brother. The Marked. I don't know who started it. I don't like that everybody already knows it.

close_05.speaker: narrator
close_05.text: Cael has not spoken since the field. He is walking with his hands pushed into his coat, and light is coming through the fabric.

close_06.speaker: narrator
close_06.text: Somewhere behind you, a long way off, something under the mountain answers the Tremor with another one.

close_07.speaker: narrator
close_07.text: It is not over. Nobody has told anyone that yet, because nobody knows it, but every one of you felt the ground agree with it.
